transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2025-05-21 09:30 PDT
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Patel, Maya Chen, Victor Alvarez (Redwood); Lena Morales, Omar Siddiqui, Priya Rao, Ben Carter (Nimbus)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect)
Nimbus is close to staging greenlight; outstanding security items discussed. Agreed to run a short performance test to validate latency under realistic traffic and to finalize KMS keys exchange.

[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick check — did the calendar time change for anyone?
[00:08] Lena Morales: No, we're good. apologies i had a quick stand that overran but i'm here.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Awesome. I'll kick us off — quick agenda: credential sprint status, staging network readiness, KMS/key access, then a short perf / batching tune conversation and next steps. Maya, anything to add?
[00:25] Maya Chen: Nope that's perfect. I'll be focusing on the credential details — we've updated the playbook after last week.
[00:29] Victor Alvarez: And I'll cover the runbook and pilot checklist.
[00:32] Ben Carter: Great. From product side, main ask is to make sure we can validate throughput at minimum 40 rps with 95th latency under 350ms for snippet generation.
[00:42] Priya Rao: And also we need to be sure the KV cache is warm for our typical prefix sizes — lots of small prompts.

[01:05] Jordan Patel: Cool. Lena, can you run through where you are on the IAM/service account side?
[01:12] Lena Morales: Sure. We created a service account, but we haven't finished the cross-account role yet. Omar and I discussed the KMS policy — Omar is going to request least-privilege key. I think the missing piece is a fully attached role that Redwood can assume for the staging cluster. We have the subnet IDs ready.
[01:31] Omar Siddiqui: Yeah, and small note — our security team wants proof of SOC2 cert and also a short diagram of the control plane access. We've seen the doc but need the updated cert snapshot and audit log retention times.
[01:45] Jordan Patel: Understood. Victor, did we already share the SOC2 packet?
[01:50] Victor Alvarez: We shared an initial packet two weeks ago; I'll resend the updated snapshot tonight and include the audit-log retention section.
[01:57] Maya Chen: For the role assumption we recommend using a short-lived STS role with external ID. That avoids long-lived keys and matches our onboarding playbook. I'll add the exact policy snippet to the doc.

[02:28] Priya Rao: Quick question — about KMS, do you need full decrypt rights or just sign? Our platform uses envelope encryption with a customer-managed key.
[02:36] Maya Chen: We need decrypt for the runtime side to unseal the model layers if you're using CMEK. If you're doing envelope and we only get an encrypted blob, Redwood's agent needs to be able to call kms:Decrypt on the key per the playbook. We can also support bringing your own HSM via our private mode but that's a slightly longer path.
[02:56] Omar Siddiqui: Okay decrypt makes sense, but we'll scope it to a very limited principal and an IAM condition on source VPC.

[03:18] Jordan Patel: Great. Let's talk staging network readiness. Lena you said subnet IDs are ready — any issues with NAT or egress?
[03:26] Lena Morales: We have constrained egress through our NAT gateway due to cost, so we prefer minimal outbound calls. Redwood recommended a VPC peering or privatelink model last week — we think privatelink is preferred.
[03:38] Maya Chen: Privatelink is supported. We'll need the endpoint DNS and route table entries. The critical part is that we can reach the gateway and that port 443 is open to our endpoint IPs. Also, if you prefer minimal egress we can package a container image in your registry to reduce outbound pulls.
[03:56] Ben Carter: Is there any extra latency when using privatelink vs public egress?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Slight, typically +5-15ms depending on region. For your 40 rps target it's negligible but we'll measure in the mini-benchmark.

[04:22] Speaker 6: [unintelligible]...

[04:30] Jordan Patel: Okay next — scheduling the mini-benchmark. We're proposing a shadow-run at 50 rps for 15 minutes with a mix of short prompts and multi-turn, to validate both latency and KV cache hit behavior. Thoughts?
[04:48] Priya Rao: That sounds good. Can we also include a worst-case set with long context to see token tail latency?
[04:54] Maya Chen: Yes we can stage two profiles: typical (short prompts) and worst-case (4k token tail). We'll provide the runner and collect metrics.

[05:10] Lena Morales: When do you want to run it? This week or next?
[05:13] Jordan Patel: Preferably next Wednesday 2025-05-28 so we have time to finish credential exchange. Lina? (sic)
[05:18] Lena Morales: Works for us.

[05:21] Omar Siddiqui: Quick compliance point — during the benchmark we need to ensure no PII leaves the staging environment; we'll use synthetic data.
[05:29] Victor Alvarez: Agreed. We'll run with your synthetic dataset and keep logs in your S3 bucket behind the IAM role.

[05:42] Maya Chen: On batching — we looked at your traffic profile Priya shared. Given short prompts and small generation lengths, a batch size of 8 with dynamic micro-batching should balance latency and cost. But for worst-case long contexts we'll reduce batch size to 4 to keep tail latency in check.
[06:05] Priya Rao: Any KV cache tuning suggestions? We've seen cold-start issues when a lot of small prefixes hit different conversation ids.
[06:13] Maya Chen: We'll enable prefix caching with a TTL of 30 minutes for your use-case and increase the KV cache memory allocation on the staging pool. Also make sure the client sends conversation IDs consistently so the cache keys align.

[06:35] Jordan Patel: There's a small item — you mentioned earlier some errors when you tried to pull our staging image. What happened?
[06:42] Lena Morales: It was an auth token issue; the registry token was rotated last week and we didn't get the new artifact. We produced a temporary workaround but we'll add the RBAC for the service account.
[06:54] Maya Chen: We'll provide the exact permission list for the registry pull in the doc tonight.

[07:05] Ben Carter: On the product SLA — once pilot is live, how quickly can we route traffic to Redwood Dedicated if we see perf regressions in hosted?
[07:14] Jordan Patel: We can standby a dedicated pool but the commitment process takes a little time; for the pilot we can do a manual failover to a higher-tier host in the hosted system and run canary rules. If you require guaranteed capacity we'll open a dedicated discuss next step with sales.
[07:34] Ben Carter: Okay that's fine for pilot.

[07:39] Speaker 6: [crosstalk] ...sounds good

[07:44] Jordan Patel: Quick note on observability — Victor will send the runbook link which contains the token-level cost view, per-route latency histograms, and trace IDs we can correlate.
[07:56] Victor Alvarez: I'll send the runbook now after the call and follow up in the doc.

[08:05] Omar Siddiqui: Do you have an example of the audit-log format we can ingest into our SIEM?
[08:11] Victor Alvarez: Yes, we output JSON logs with fields: timestamp, service, request_id, principal, action, and we can include the model version. I'll attach a sample to the runbook.
[08:25] Lena Morales: Also need to confirm log retention — we want 180 days for pilot.
[08:29] Victor Alvarez: We currently default to 90 days on hosted, but for the staging bucket we can configure 180 days. I'll note that as an item.

[08:40] Jordan Patel: Anything else on security?
[08:43] Omar Siddiqui: One more — SSO/SAML for console access. We'll need SAML config for your console team with SCIM provisioning ideally.
[08:55] Maya Chen: We support SAML and SCIM; I'll send the SSO guide with attributes and sample metadata. SCIM can be enabled after an initial admin user is created.

[09:06] Priya Rao: From ML side, once we run the benchmark I'd like to iterate on the quantization profile. We saw a tiny delta in quality between q4 and q8 in our internal tests — need to validate live.
[09:19] Maya Chen: We can run two model variants in the benchmark — one with conservative quant and one with more aggressive q4. We'll tag requests so your eval harness can compare.

[09:32] Jordan Patel: Great — seems like action items are clear. Quick recap: Maya to update docs and policy snippets; Victor to resend SOC2 and runbook; Lena to provide subnet and IAM ARNs; Omar to scope KMS policy; agreed mini-benchmark 2025-05-28 with synthetic data. Any objections?
[09:52] Ben Carter: No objections.

[09:56] Lena Morales: One last ask — can Redwood share a short checklist we can hand to our network team for privatelink? They like short checkboxes.
[10:04] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll add a one-page privatelink checklist to the playbook.

[10:10] Jordan Patel: Perfect. We'll follow up with the doc and action items. Thanks everyone, see you next week.

[10:20] (end of recording)

Post-call notes:
- Minor transcription artifacts: "privatelink" sometimes transcribed as "private link"; "KV cache" appeared as "KVM cache" in one place.
- Links referenced during call (to be attached in email): staging-credential-playbook.md, redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf, pilot-runbook-v1.2.md

Recap (email-suitable):
Jordan to coordinate; Maya updates the credential/playbook; Victor resends compliance packet; Nimbus to deliver IAM/KMS details; mini-benchmark scheduled 2025-05-28.
